turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
**My predicted ranking is c064, c005, c017, c013, c043.** I prioritize high-performing measured analogues, then consider whether the changes preserve selective extraction, suppress interfacial recombination, and support a continuous absorber film. These are predictions of configuration-median efficiency—not measured efficiencies for the candidates.

| Rank | Candidate | Training evidence and device-physics rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **c064** | **TiO2-c / SnO2-np / Spiro-MeOTAD / Au** has the strongest ETL precedent: the same oxide stack with Ag and spin-coating followed by dip-coating reaches **20.85%**. A related TiO2-c / SnO2 stack achieves **17.47%** with ordinary spin-coating. Compact TiO2 provides electron selectivity and blocks electrode–absorber leakage; the SnO2 overlayer can improve electron extraction and the absorber-facing interface. Spiro-MeOTAD/Au supplies a well-established hole-selective contact. I would not transfer the full 20.85% result, because the deposition procedure differs. |
| **2** | **c005** | Its TiO2-c / PCBM-60 ETL, polymer HTL, MoO3 / Au contact, and sequential spin-coating closely resemble the **19.35%** PCDTBT1 training device. PCBM can cover oxide surface defects and reduce electron-side recombination, while MoO3 can facilitate hole collection at the polymer/metal contact. The main uncertainty is **PCDTBT8 versus PCDTBT1**: their energy levels, mobility, and film morphology cannot be assumed identical. |
| **3** | **c017** | The nearly identical fullerene / doped-TaTm configuration with Au achieves **17.9%**. Fullerene electron selectivity, a conductive F6-TCNNQ-doped hole-contact region, and co-evaporated absorber formation give this candidate an unusually direct high-efficiency precedent. Replacing Au with Ag introduces contact-work-function and chemical-stability uncertainty, but the intervening hole-transport stack makes this less concerning than direct Ag–perovskite contact. |
| **4** | **c013** | This retains the TiO2-c / modified-Spiro-MeOTAD / MoO3 / Ag backbone represented by the **18.965%** IEICO-4F-modified training device. P(VDF-TrFE) offers a plausible route to interfacial electrostatic modification and reduced recombination. This is a **functional analogy**, not an equivalent modifier: a thick insulating polymer layer would instead impede hole extraction. |
| **5** | **c043** | The compact/mesoporous TiO2 / interlayer / Spiro-MeOTAD / Au configuration is supported by **18.01%** for PMMA / Spiro-MeOTAD and **16.15%** for graphene oxide / Spiro-MeOTAD. The DAHI interlayer offers a plausible interface-engineering route while retaining established extraction contacts. Its precise chemistry and coverage are not specified, making this selection less secure than the first three. |

The first three have the strongest direct training support. The last two depend more on whether their interlayers passivate the absorber without adding a transport barrier; the supplied process labels do not resolve that uncertainty.

Final: c064, c005, c017, c013, c043
